preamble: Several solutions, not defined in their clues, are of a kind

clue.text: One's warmed by this shoot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hearth blaze you sit beside to get warm
second meaning: to start firing guns

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one sentence about being warmed by a shoot, but they are separate meanings of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an uncovered domestic blaze in a grate and the military command to begin shooting.

clue.text: First to introduce gospel, missionary aims to follow St Mark

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first of each word is wanted, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A missionary sets out to bring the gospel to people, following in the footsteps of St Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Mark' looks like the gospel writer, but the saint's abbreviation is a piece of wordplay and 'Mark' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a visible sign or stain, including a mark of shame or the wounds of Christ.

clue.text: Man on board reported no time for sleep?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how it is spoken

parts.note: a white knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: Someone on a board of directors claims they had no time to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a company director, but it is a chessman; the K of the chess piece is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A white night is a sleepless night, one spent wide awake without any rest, so the question mark flags a phrase.

clue.text: Like a wolf that bears flowers with the end to seduce

parts.note: the lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of flowers

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of 'seduce'

explanation.surface: A predatory wolf comes bearing flowers in an effort to seduce someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a wolf as a womaniser; the plant name is taken from the Latin for wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine is the adjective relating to wolves, built from Latin lupus, just as canine relates to dogs.

clue.text: One patient needing a bath? Someone's gotta do it!

definitions.note: a quotation standing for the thing that must be done, a noun phrase

parts.note: someone needing a bath is unwashed
the biblical Job is proverbial for his patience

explanation.surface: A hospital patient needs bathing, and a nurse grumbles that someone has to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as a hospital patient, but it is the adjective: the patience of Job is proverbial. The definition quotes 'It's a dirty job, but someone's gotta do it.'
explanation.definitionFit: The saying refers to an unpleasant task that nobody wants but which must still be done by somebody.

clue.text: Copy covering the start of summer recess

indicators.note: to cover something is to sit around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to ape is to imitate

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'summer'

explanation.surface: Someone copies homework to cover the summer holidays from school or parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer recess' reads as a holiday break, but recess here is an architectural alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular alcove, typically at the east end of a church, so it is an architectural recess.

clue.text: Work from 16 as nation developed

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so these letters take a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patriotic piece by a composer grew as the nation itself developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is ELGAR, a fitting cross-reference since Elgar is famed for patriotic music; the definition needs the 16 answer to read fully.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonatina is a short, light sonata, a musical composition of the kind Elgar wrote for piano.

clue.text: See 23
Even slices of apple pie have a filling that's a touch strange

indicators.note: something with a filling holds another piece inside it, like a sandwich
even-numbered portions mean the second, fourth and so on of each word are kept

parts.note: the even letters of each word: P and L of 'apple', I of 'pie'

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slice of apple pie has a slightly odd-tasting filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's 'of a kind' is scents: this answer has no definition in the clue. 'A touch strange' looks like a description of the taste but is the scrambled filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavy aromatic oil from an Asian shrub, used in perfumes, so it belongs with the other scents.

clue.text: Top house design no use in picture

indicators.note: a design is a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh
'no' means without, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, to be taken away

explanation.surface: A top architect's house design proves useless when it appears in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip USE from the end of 'house' to leave HO, then rearrange it with TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Photo is the everyday short form of photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: After dark, I'm heading west wearing tattered jeans

parts.note: the dark part of the day

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means running right to left, so the letters run backwards
whatever is worn sits inside clothing, so one piece goes within another
tattered means ragged and torn apart, so the letters are pulled into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After dark someone heads out west wearing ripped jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the undefined scents the preamble mentions. 'After dark' looks like a time phrase, but the dark itself gives the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Night jasmine is a shrub whose small white flowers release a strong perfume after dusk, making it one of the scents.

clue.text: Cryptic hint, what with bird being worth double here?

definitions.note: a description of the place where a bird is worth two, answered by a prepositional phrase

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure and puzzling, so the letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
eh? is a way of saying 'what?' when you have not heard
and means together with

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's hint, all about a bird that is worth twice as much in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush'; 'worth double' is the two in the bush, and the answer is where the one bird sits. 'Cryptic' looks like a comment on the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that something already possessed is worth twice as much as a bigger prize merely hoped for.

clue.text: Member of the family may be earning

indicators.note: 'may be' suggests the letters could turn into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One relative in the household might be the breadwinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' reads as a hedge about who is earning, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A grannie, a variant spelling of granny, is a grandmother, one of the relatives in a family.

clue.text: I go my way, being of a different persuasion

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase; the answer is a plural noun for people of that persuasion

indicators.note: doing something one's own way means arranging it differently, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists on going their own way because they hold a different belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'I did it my way'; the definition is a description of the people, so the answer is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Goyim is the Yiddish and Hebrew term for gentiles, people who are not Jewish and so follow another faith.

clue.text: See 11
Silence ego?

parts.note: surface reading: an order to hush someone's self-importance
setter's reading: split it as E.G. plus O; e.g. means 'for example' and O is zero

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer phrase describes how to build 'ego'. Take 'say' as e.g. and 'nothing' as O, and the two words of the answer spell the clue's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep quiet and offer no remark at all is to remain silent, so the phrase means silence as a verb.

clue.text: Last night of the Proms feature in hotel garden

definitions.text: Last night of the Proms feature

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, straddling the gap between them

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A highlight of the Last Night of the Proms is staged in a hotel garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms is a summer season of London concerts whose rowdy Last Night always includes Elgar's 'Land of Hope and Glory'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Pomp and Circumstance March No 1 is a fixture of the Last Night, so the composer is a regular feature.

clue.text: Would have been a great pianist, if it weren't for the Yankees

parts.note: Yankee is the radio-alphabet code word for the letter Y; the plural gives two of them
Lang Lang is a celebrated Chinese concert pianist
the second of the two code-word letters
the second half of the pianist's name
surface padding framing the joke: without the Ys the answer would be the pianist
surface padding: the Ys are what stop it being the pianist's name

explanation.surface: An American sports fan laments that the Yankees spoiled a fine musical career.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: remove the two Ys from the answer and you are left with the pianist Lang Lang. The New York Yankees suggest baseball but they are the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ylang-ylang is a fragrant oil from the flowers of a tropical Asian tree, widely used in perfumery.

clue.text: Marriage of pin-up in fancy lace

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
one piece goes inside the other
fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a nail is a kind of pin

explanation.surface: A wedding features a glamorous pin-up model dressed in fancy lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' looks like a single word for a model, but it splits into a pin and an upward direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or bond, and a marriage alliance is a union between families through wedlock.

clue.text: Throw light on bald heads

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A lamp shines on men's bald heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw light on' reads as a phrase meaning explain, but 'Throw' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To lob is to toss something in a high, gentle arc, so it is a kind of throw.

clue.text: John Terminator

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, as is lav in Britain
something that terminates puts an end to things

explanation.surface: It looks like a name: a man called John who is a Terminator, perhaps a film credit.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like names from the Terminator films, but 'John' is a toilet and 'Terminator' is one who ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a purple-flowered herb whose oil is one of the best-known scents in soaps and perfumes.

clue.text: See 17
Bravo to Lombardy serving a retro cocktail

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes before 'cocktail' in the name of the weapon

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters run the other way
what is served is held out within something, so the answer lies inside these words

parts.note: from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A bar in Lombardy is praised for serving an old-fashioned cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo' and 'retro cocktail' suggest a bar scene; the definition is a petrol bomb, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Molotov cocktail is a home-made incendiary bomb named after the Soviet minister, so the name completes that phrase.

clue.text: Promote spoons bent by Geller at the end

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of 'Geller'

explanation.surface: Uri Geller, the showman famous for bending spoons, is used to promote something.
explanation.walkthrough: Geller's spoon-bending act makes 'bent' look literal; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor something is to back it with money or support, which promotes it publicly.

clue.text: Little money in Swiss banks

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the banks of a river are its two edges, so the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'Swiss'
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: A small amount of cash is deposited in Swiss banks.
explanation.walkthrough: This names the kind the preamble refers to: the undefined answers are all scents. 'Swiss banks' looks like a financial phrase, but banks means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: The undefined themed answers are all perfumes and aromatic oils, things valued for their pleasant smells.

clue.text: Public disgrace to ignore second court order, essentially

indicators.note: ignoring the second letter means leaving it out

parts.note: a scandal is a public disgrace
to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of 'order'

explanation.surface: A public scandal arises because someone ignored a second court order.
explanation.walkthrough: Another undefined scent. 'Court order' looks like a legal phrase, but 'court' means woo and 'order' gives only its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandalwood is a fragrant timber from an Indian tree whose oil is prized in incense and perfume.

clue.text: Le Figaro?

parts.note: the French article places us in France
Le Figaro is a French newspaper, and rag is slang for a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: Le Figaro is a French daily, so it is a rag in France; read 'in' as putting one inside the other. The answer is another word for the theme itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, the general kind to which all the undefined perfume answers belong.

clue.text: See 1
Stood up to recite lines
Anne Hathaway's head, back and hair treatment

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of 'Hathaway's'; that the result also lies reversed across 'Anne Hathaway's' is a coincidence of this same parse

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife Anne Hathaway, or the actress, has her head and back treated along with her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' and 'back' read as body parts in a spa list, but each is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye from a shrub's leaves, used to colour and condition hair.

clue.text: State slavery not clever

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave something out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
sly means cunning or clever

explanation.surface: A political statement that slavery is not a clever policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation in the surface; it is the verb. The removed letters are scattered: S and L at the front, Y at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert something firmly as true, so it means to state.

clue.text: Geology subject is awesome!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the stones geologists study
second meaning: slang verb for being excellent

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an enthusiastic student praising geology; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones and minerals are what geologists study, and in slang something that is brilliant is said to be great.

clue.text: Unwrapped sexy item, one out later to lessen the impact

indicators.note: unwrapping strips off the outer layer, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the inside of 'sexy'
the inside of 'item'
the inside of 'one'
the inside of 'out'
the inside of 'later'

explanation.surface: A sexy item is unwrapped, one taken out later to soften the blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The words after 'Unwrapped' look like a story but are just a string of words to strip; 'one out' tempts a solver to drop an I.
explanation.definitionFit: To extenuate an offence is to make it seem less serious, reducing the force of the blame.
